chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

That Ali (peace be upon him) used to say regarding a man who divorces his wife with one divorce, then marries her again after a husband [from whom she had three divorces or another husband], 'Indeed, she is with him upon whatever remained of her divorces.'

key_terms.بَعْدَ زَوْجٍ: after a husband (implying a subsequent marriage or the count of divorces)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on remarriage after a single divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) established that upon remarriage after a single revocable divorce (taliqah), the wife remains under the status of the remaining two divorces, a ruling that clarifies the continuity of the three-divorce limit. This narration, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to al-Sadiq, highlights the practical application of the 'one divorce' rule in early Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the finality of the third divorce. It underscores the principle that remarriage does not erase the previous divorce count but rather continues the tally towards the final separation.
